29157-the-coinages-of-the-channel-island.title: Channel Islands.
29157-the-coinages-of-the-channel-island.creator: Unknown
29157-the-coinages-of-the-channel-island.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The earliest inhabitants of the islands of whom anything is known were contemporaneous with the ancient Britons of Druidical times. Jersey and Guernsey are still rich in Druidical remains. The Table-stone of the Cromlech at Gorey is 160 feet superficial, and the weight, as I have made it, after careful calculation, is about 23-3/4 tons.

arxiv-1903-11932.title: The undecidability of joint embedding and joint homomorphism for hereditary graph classes
arxiv-1903-11932.creator: Samuel Braunfeld
arxiv-1903-11932.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Samuel Braunfeld. We prove that the joint embedding property is undecidable for hereditary graph classes, via a reduction from the tiling problem. The proof is then adapted to show the undecidability of the joint homomorphism property as well. \publicationdetails 212019295325 † † accepted: Accepted: 2019-11-20 1 Introduction A hereditary class {\mathcal{C}} of structures has the joint embedding property (JEP) if, given A,B\in{\mathcal{C}} , there exists C\in{\mathcal{C}} such that A,B embed into C .

arxiv-2107-00456.title: Crowdsourcing Evaluation of Saliency-based XAI Methods
arxiv-2107-00456.creator: Xiaotian Lu ✉, Arseny Tolmachev, Tatsuya Yamamoto, Koh Takeuchi, Seiji Okajima, Tomoyoshi Takebayashi, Koji Maruhashi, Hisashi Kashima
arxiv-2107-00456.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Xiaotian Lu ✉, Arseny Tolmachev, Tatsuya Yamamoto, Koh Takeuchi, Seiji Okajima, Tomoyoshi Takebayashi, Koji Maruhashi, Hisashi Kashima. Understanding the reasons behind the predictions made by deep neural networks is critical for gaining human trust in many important applications, which is reflected in the increasing demand for explainability in AI (XAI) in recent years. Saliency-based feature attribution methods, which highlight important parts of images that contribute to decisions by classifiers, are often used as XAI methods, especially in the field of computer vision.

arxiv-2205-00710.creator: Arup Kumar Paul 1 , Manas Ranjan Sahu 1 , Kenji Watanabe 2 , Takashi Taniguchi 2 , J. K. Jain 3 , Ganpathy Murthy 4,⋆ , and Anindya Das 1,†
arxiv-2205-00710.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Arup Kumar Paul 1 , Manas Ranjan Sahu 1 , Kenji Watanabe 2 , Takashi Taniguchi 2 , J. K. Jain 3 , Ganpathy Murthy 4,⋆ , and Anindya Das 1,†. The ground state of a graphene sheet at charge neutrality in a perpendicular magnetic field remains enigmatic, with various experiments supporting canted antiferromagnetic, bond ordered, and even charge density wave phases.

arxiv-2305-04171.title: Regularity of the Siciak-Zaharjuta extremal function on compact Kähler manifolds
arxiv-2305-04171.creator: Ngoc Cuong Nguyen
arxiv-2305-04171.description: Abstract . We prove that the regularity of the extremal function of a compact subset of a compact Kähler manifold is a local property, and that the continuity and Hölder continuity are equivalent to classical notions of the local L L -regularity and the locally Hölder continuous property in pluripotential theory.

arxiv-2310-14240.title: An extremely bad-cavity laser
arxiv-2310-14240.creator: Jia Zhang 1, Tiantian Shi 1,2,3, Jianxiang Miao 1, Deshui Yu 4, Jingbiao Chen 1,5
arxiv-2310-14240.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jia Zhang 1, Tiantian Shi 1,2,3, Jianxiang Miao 1, Deshui Yu 4, Jingbiao Chen 1,5. Lasing in the bad-cavity regime has promising applications in precision measurement and frequency metrology due to the reduced sensitivity of the laser frequency to cavity length fluctuations. Thus far, relevant studies have been mainly focused on conventional cavities whose finesse is high enough that the resonance linewidth is sufficiently narrow compared to the cavity’s free spectral range, though still in the bad-cavity regime.

arxiv-2312-02432.title: Orthogonal Adaptation for Modular Customization of Diffusion Models
arxiv-2312-02432.creator: Ryan Po, Guandao Yang, Kfir Aberman, Gordon Wetzstein
arxiv-2312-02432.description: Abstract Customization techniques for text-to-image models have paved the way for a wide range of previously unattainable applications, enabling the generation of specific concepts across diverse contexts and styles. While existing methods facilitate high-fidelity customization for individual concepts or a limited, pre-defined set of them, they fall short of achieving scalability, where a single model can seamlessly render countless concepts.

arxiv-2503-23503.title: Evolutionary Prompt Optimization Discovers Emergent Multimodal Reasoning Strategies in Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2503-23503.creator: Sid Bharthulwar, John Rho, Katrina Brown
arxiv-2503-23503.description: Abstract We present a framework for optimizing prompts in vision-language models to elicit multimodal reasoning without model retraining. Using an evolutionary algorithm to guide prompt updates downstream of visual tasks, our approach improves upon baseline prompt-updating algorithms, which lack evolution-style ”survival of the fittest” iteration.

arxiv-2512-22443.title: Exploring the Vertical-Domain Reasoning Capabilities of Large Language Models
arxiv-2512-22443.creator: Jie Zhou, Xin Chen, Jie Zhang, Zhe Li
arxiv-2512-22443.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are reshaping learning paradigms, cognitive processes, and research methodologies across a wide range of domains. Integrating LLMs with professional fields and redefining the relationship between LLMs and domain-specific applications has become a critical challenge for promoting enterprise digital transformation and broader social development.

pmc-10525320.title: Transcriptome Studies Reveal the N6-Methyladenosine Differences in Testis of Yaks at Juvenile and Sexual Maturity Stages
pmc-10525320.creator: Shaoke Guo, Jie Pei, Xingdong Wang, Mengli Cao, Lin Xiong, Yandong Kang, Ziqiang Ding, Yongfu La, Min Chu, Pengjia Bao, Xian Guo
pmc-10525320.description: Simple SummaryThe methylation level of testicular tissue in young yaks and adult yaks was determined, and the N6-methyladenosine (m6A) level was significantly increased after sexual maturity. Functional enrichment analysis of differentially methylated mRNAs screened between the two groups after sequencing showed that they mainly regulated cell development, spermatogenesis, and testicular endocrine function.

pmc-10561337.title: Rationale of the PAPAartis trial
pmc-10561337.creator: Martin Misfeld, Josephina Haunschild, David Petroff, Michael A Borger, Christian D Etz
pmc-10561337.description: Surgical and interventional repair of thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms improve survival significantly compared to the natural history of the disease. However, both strategies are associated with a substantial risk of spinal cord ischemia, which has been reported to occur—even in contemporary series by expert centers—in up to 12% of patients, depending on the extent of the disease.

pmc-10565009.title: Potential efficacy of dopaminergic antidepressants in treatment resistant anergic-anhedonic depression results of the chronic anergic-anhedonic depression open trial – CADOT
pmc-10565009.creator: Ludovic Christophe Dormegny-Jeanjean, Clément de Billy, Olivier Mainberger, Sébastien Weibel, Benoit Schorr, Alexandre Obrecht, Lionel Landré, Fabrice Berna, Jean-Baptiste Causin, Frederic Blanc, Vlad Danila, Mihaela Tomsa, Geraldine Pfleger, Camille Meyer, Ilia Humbert, Hervé Javelot, Guillaume Mey
pmc-10565009.description: IntroductionAmong treatment-resistant depression (TRD), we identified anergic-anhedonic clinical presentations (TRAD) as putatively responsive to pro-dopaminergic strategies. Based on the literature, non-selective monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOI) and dopamine D2 receptor agonists (D2RAG) were sequentially introduced, frequently under the coverage of a mood stabilizer. This two-step therapeutic strategy will be referred to as the Dopaminergic Antidepressant Therapy Algorithm (DATA).

pmc-11709835.title: Peripheral Signatures of Disease Heterogeneity
pmc-11709835.creator: Lenora A Higginbotham
pmc-11709835.description: BackgroundThere is currently an unmet need for novel accessible biomarkers that capture the complex and heterogenous pathophysiology of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Over the past decade, the systems‐based multi‐omic approaches employed by the Accelerating Medicines Partnership in AD (AMP‐AD) have resulted in the identification of promising peripheral markers of disease heterogeneity.

pmc-12533530.title: Autism spectrum disorder: communicative profile before and after remote family guidance
pmc-12533530.creator: Leonara Emanuelle Honório Silva, Denise Brandão de Oliveira e Britto, Leonara Emanuelle Honório Silva, Denise Brandão de Oliveira e Britto
pmc-12533530.description: PurposeTo compare the communicative profile of children diagnosed with or at risk for autism spectrum disorder before and after speech-language-hearing guidance (indirect treatment).MethodsThe study included caregivers and/or parents of children aged 2 to 9 years with a diagnosis of or at risk for autism spectrum disorder, with or without speech-language-hearing therapy.

pmc-13330136.title: Population Pharmacokinetic, Exposure‐Response Efficacy and Safety Analyses of Favezelimab in Patients With Solid Tumors
pmc-13330136.creator: Mitali Gaurav, Heather Barcomb, Kelly F. Maxwell, Bhargava Kandala, Manash S. Chatterjee
pmc-13330136.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Favezelimab (MK‐4280) is a humanized monoclonal antibody (mAb) targeting lymphocyte activation gene‐3 (LAG‐3). Favezelimab population pharmacokinetics (popPK) was evaluated using data from 2 trials; a Phase 1 study evaluating favezelimab across a range of doses (7 to 800 mg administered intravenously [IV] every 3 weeks [Q3W]) in patients with advanced solid tumors, and a Phase 3 study evaluating 800 mg IV Q3W favezelimab combined with pembrolizumab (200 mg Q3W) in patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD‐L1) positive colorectal cancer (CRC).

pmc-13378150.creator: Xiaotang Xia, Yulin Xu, Jian Chen
pmc-13378150.description: SummaryThis study proposes an enhanced remote sensing ecological index (ERSEI) incorporating water-retention dynamics to quantify spatiotemporal variations in ecological quality and carbon storage in Yichang city (2003–2023). Utilizing principal-component analysis (PCA) and GeoDetector, we evaluated ERSEI trajectories and underlying mechanisms. Results reveal that mean ERSEI increased by approximately 12.

pmc-13549637.title: Tobacco and alcohol use, fruit and vegetable consumption, physical activity habits, and participation in routine checkups and cancer screenings among adults aged 40 and older with and without chronic diseases
pmc-13549637.creator: Elif Nur Yildirim-Ozturk, Mehmet Uyar
pmc-13549637.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The study aimed to investigate tobacco and alcohol use, fruit and vegetable consumption, physical activity habits, and participation in routine checkups and cancer screenings in adults aged 40 years and older with and without a diagnosis of chronic disease. It also aimed to compare the frequentist and Bayesian statistical methods used for comparisons and to evaluate the practical significance of these associations using effect sizes. The study was cross-sectional.

pmc-13575186.title: Quantifying the role of nitrogen in achieving global Sustainable Development Goals
pmc-13575186.creator: Yi Zhou, Xiuming Zhang, Yiyang Zou, Chen Wang, Xin Xu, Baojing Gu
pmc-13575186.description: Achieving the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) requires balancing well-being with environmental protection, yet the role of nitrogen across these goals remains poorly understood. Here, we show how dietary nitrogen intake and nitrogen release to air and water are associated with SDG progress across 166 countries from 2000 to 2022.

pmc-13682149.title: Socioeconomic transitions and the spatial dynamics of syphilis transmission in urbanizing China
pmc-13682149.creator: Chengcheng Li, Hanxi Zhang, Jinfeng Li, Ximan Ye, Shangcheng Zhou, Xiaojie Lao, Maowei Chen
pmc-13682149.description: BackgroundSyphilis remains a re-emerging sexually transmitted infection in China, with transmission increasingly shaped by regional socioeconomic disparities. Understanding spatial heterogeneity and inter-provincial inequality is essential for equitable disease control.MethodsA balanced panel dataset of syphilis incidence was constructed across 31 provinces in mainland China from 2004 to 2020. Temporal trends were stratified by age and disease stage using joinpoint regression analysis.
